docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• One dashboard

    Home for what is new, playing, or needs a look. Catalog for install, start/stop, and Open UI.

  • Automation + libraries

    Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and Bazarr — when you want them.

  • Downloads

    Torrents and Usenet clients, optional VPN on the download path.

  • Watch & request

    Jellyfin, Plex, and Seerr — same appliance.

The one rule: one AIO install = one container (or one native service). Do not add separate Sonarr/Radarr/qBittorrent containers next to it.

docs.title: Intended use
docs.text:
AIO is a self-hosting management tool for a personal media library and a home lab:

  • Files you own (home videos, family photos, public-domain media, or your own backups of physical media).
  • Local network setup and server administration.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Get AIO running in three steps: create folders, start the app, open the dashboard.

Prefer a short path?

Most people start with Docker or their NAS guide (Unraid · Synology · TrueNAS), then come back here for ports and updates.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
1. Pick where it will run — Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS, plain Docker, or native Linux.
  2. Plan two kinds of storage:
  3. Config — settings and databases (small, back this up)
  4. Downloads + media — the big files (keep these on the same disk/share so hardlinks work)
  5. Know your user ID — on Linux/NAS, apps often run as a specific user (PUID / PGID). Match that to who owns your folders so you do not get permission errors.

You only need one AIO container. Do not install Sonarr, Radarr, or download clients as separate apps alongside it.

Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest Architectures: linux/amd64, linux/arm64 (Flaresolverr is x86_64-only and hidden on ARM)

docs.title: Choose your platform
docs.text:
Where you run it Guide Docker (any host) Docker Unraid Unraid Synology Synology TrueNAS SCALE TrueNAS Debian / Ubuntu / Proxmox LXC (no Docker) Linux All options listed Deploy overview

Each platform guide starts with: open SSH → create folders → start AIO.

docs.title: Folders on the host
docs.text:
SSH in, then create something like this (paths vary by platform — follow your guide):

ssh user@host

mkdir -p "$HOME/aio-media-manager/downloads" "$HOME/aio-media-manager/media"
sudo mkdir -p /path/to/config /path/to/config/vpn /path/to/backups
id   # note uid= (PUID) and gid= (PGID)
sudo chown -R "$PUID:$PGID" "$HOME/aio-media-manager" /path/to/config /path/to/backups

Keep downloads and media as siblings under one folder so *Arr can hardlink. Mount a separate backups folder at /backups if you can (ideally another disk than config).

Inside those mounts AIO lays out libraries such as media/tv, media/movies, and downloads/complete.

docs.title: After it starts
docs.text:
1. Open the dashboard: http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080 (Use a different port if you mapped one.)
  2. Create the admin account (username, email, password).
  3. Complete the first-run wizard, then follow Using the dashboard.

After docker compose pull, recreate the container (not only restart) so new ports and runtimes apply. That updates AIO. Installed apps update from Settings → Updates inside the dashboard. Those schedules default to off.

The repo compose file mounts host /sys read-only at /host/sys, so Home's Server card counts the server's network cards. An older compose file without that line shows only the container's own traffic until you add it and recreate. See Docker.

docs.title: Optional: reach apps from outside your home
docs.text:
1. Cloudflare Tunnel — HTTPS without opening router ports
  2. Cloudflare Access — login gate so strangers cannot open admin apps

docs.title: Ports
docs.text:
The manager UI uses 8080. Child apps listen inside the same container. Compose and NAS templates publish those ports on the host so Open UI works (http://YOUR-IP:8989 for Sonarr, and so on). Host networking is an alternative if you prefer not to map each port.

Application Default port Manager UI 8080 qBittorrent 8081 Shelfmark 8084 SABnzbd 8085 Jellyfin 8096 Flaresolverr 8191 (x86_64 only) Bazarr 6767 NZBGet 6789 Lidarr 8686 Sonarr 8989 Radarr 7878 Prowlarr 9696 Seerr 5055 Grimmory 6060 NeutArr 9705 Recyclarr none (CLI only) Plex 32400

docs.title: Common environment variables
docs.text:
Copy .env.example for native installs. Many of these can also be set later in Settings.

Variable Purpose PUID / PGID User the apps run as (match folder ownership) TZ / AMM_TIMEZONE Timezone for logs and schedules AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR / AMM_MEDIA_DIR Paths inside the container (change host mounts in compose) GITHUB_TOKEN Optional; higher GitHub API limits for updates AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_* Optional remote tunnel (cloudflared starts after apps on boot) AMM_VPN_* Optional VPN for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr (they wait for the tunnel; local DNS cache for those apps)

docs.title: If something goes wrong
docs.text:
• Cannot open the UI — container running? Correct host port?
  • Permission denied — folder ownership must match PUID/PGID.
  • Child Open UI fails on LAN — publish that app’s port (table above) or use host networking; old compose files that only mapped 8080 need updating.
  • Apps duplicated — remove separate Sonarr/Radarr containers; only AIO should run them.

docs.title: Using the dashboard
docs.text:
This guide is for after AIO is installed and you can open the web UI.

Goal

Finish the wizard for the apps you need, use Home day to day, and use Open UI on Catalog whenever you want that tool’s screen.

Default address on your home network:

http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080

Replace the IP (and port, if you changed it).

docs.title: First time
docs.text:
1. Create the admin account when prompted (username, email, password).
  2. Finish the first-run wizard: the apps you want, a Usenet server if you use one, optional VPN, and an optional Cloudflare Tunnel. The wizard installs that selection. The tunnel and the VPN start as soon as it finishes, when you turned them on.
  3. After a container recreate, the dashboard answers while apps are still starting. With VPN on, qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr wait until the WireGuard handshake is up (AIO retries the VPN if the first try fails). Cloudflare Tunnel starts last, after the apps answer, so cloudflared does not log connection refused against origins that are not listening yet.
  4. Wait until Catalog shows those apps as running. Use Open UI for anything that still has its own account (Plex, Jellyfin, NZBGet).
  5. Add more later from Catalog. You do not need every app.

Start small (for example Radarr + one download client + Jellyfin), then add the rest.

docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Home is a grid. Phone, tablet, and desktop each keep their own layout (4, 8, and 12 columns). The layout control on the Home tab moves, resizes, adds, and removes widgets. Settings → Homepage shows or hides the app dock, sets the sign-in message, and holds a Jellyfin or Seerr API key when Home cannot read one itself.

Widget What it shows Greeting Time of day Search Seerr search Calendar Upcoming episodes and movies. A season that lands on one day is one entry Downloading Active downloads, with pause all / resume all. Stuck items can be removed Recently added New shows and movies. Scrolling loads further Jellyfin pages. Plex stays on its latest 20 Requests Seerr requests that are not finished, plus ones marked available or declined in the last 30 days Trending Seerr's trending list. Scrolling keeps loading Now playing Who is watching on Jellyfin or Plex, including direct play Storage Disk use for config, downloads, and media Server CPU, memory, and network. With host /sys mounted at /host/sys, this is the server's network cards. Without that mount it is only this container's traffic Needs attention The same checks as Settings → Notifications, with a link to fix each one Other downloads Off by default; add it from the layout control. What SABnzbd, NZBGet, and qBittorrent downloaded that is not a film or series (music, books, games, software, archives), each with an icon for its kind

Install, start, stop, and Open UI live on Catalog. The dock at the bottom of Home opens apps that are already installed.

LAN Open UI usually looks like http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8989 (example for Sonarr). If you set up Cloudflare public hostnames, Open UI can instead use https://sonarr.yourdomain.com — see Cloudflare Tunnel.

docs.title: What the wizard wires
docs.text:
After an app is healthy — or when you click Auto-Wire — AIO sets download folders and categories, root folders and download clients in Sonarr, Radarr, and Lidarr, Prowlarr sync, Seerr, Bazarr pairing, and starter configs for Recyclarr and NeutArr. Settings → Usenet holds the news server and sends it to SABnzbd and NZBGet. Prowlarr also gets a starter set of public indexers. Remove any you do not want; they are not added back.

Keep downloads and media on the same volume so completed files can hardlink.

Still yours to finish:

  • A Plex account.
  • NeutArr's first-run setup token (below), until that account exists.
  • Signing in to Jellyfin and NZBGet. On the LAN, Open UI already signs in Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, Bazarr, and Seerr as the manager admin. Public hostnames always show the app's own login.
  • Seerr's admin and first-run wizard are completed for you from that shared login (through Jellyfin, or a claimed Plex).

VPN, Cloudflare Tunnel, Recyclarr, NeutArr, and backups are optional.

docs.title: NeutArr first-run setup token
docs.text:
The first time NeutArr starts, before it has an account, it asks for a one-time setup token.

  1. Wait until NeutArr shows as running.
  2. Open Catalog → NeutArr → Settings.
  3. Copy First-run setup token and paste it into NeutArr's setup screen.

That value is the file /config/neutarr/.setup-token inside the appliance (the host folder mounted as /config). NeutArr deletes the file after the account is created, and the Settings field goes empty. Until NeutArr has started, the field stays empty.

docs.title: Opening each app’s UI
docs.text:
Situation What to use At home on Wi‑Fi Open UI → http://IP:PORT Away from home with Cloudflare Open UI → https://subdomain.yourdomain.com You changed an app’s listen port AIO updates published routes; recreate the container if LAN links still look wrong. The manager port itself is compose/env (AMM_API_PORT), shown on Settings → System

If Open UI fails:

  • Is the app running on Catalog?
  • Are you on the same network (for LAN links)?
  • For HTTPS links: is the tunnel connected and was Publish successful? (Cloudflare guide)

docs.text:
Names in the UI may be short labels; here is what they mean in practice.

Section Why it matters Account Admin username, email, and password. Apps that take a local login use the same account Visuals Theme, accent, wallpaper, title, header icon, login logo, and favicon System Timezone, log level, PUID/PGID, and the AIO version. Storage paths are shown here; change the mounts in compose, not in this screen. The manager listen port is compose/env only Updates Check and apply updates for installed apps, one at a time or all at once. Schedules default to off. A newer AIO image is a notice only — pull and recreate on the host Backups Config backup, verify, per-app restore, and a schedule Network VPN for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr (Usenet stays off it), with a local DNS cache for those apps so short tunnel hiccups do not knock Prowlarr indexers offline; Cloudflare Tunnel (starts after apps on boot); public subdomains; and trusted proxies Notifications Discord webhook and email when an app crash-loops, the VPN or tunnel drops, an update is available, or a disk passes 90% full Usenet News server (host, port, SSL, login, connections), sent to SABnzbd and NZBGet. NZB indexers are added in Prowlarr Homepage Sign-in message, app dock, and Jellyfin / Seerr API keys when Home cannot read them Diagnostics Why a Home widget is empty. API keys are never shown. docs.title: Updating apps vs updating AIO
docs.text:
What How AIO itself (dashboard + supervisor) Pull a new Docker image and recreate the container (Install). Settings → Updates only tells you when :latest moved Installed apps (Sonarr, Seerr, and the rest) Settings → Updates. Update one app or all of them. Progress shows there, and Catalog and Home show Updating…. The dashboard keeps answering. Schedules default to off

The image does not bump those apps on its own. Read release notes on GitHub if something major changed.

docs.title: Common snags
docs.text: Problem Try this Blank or login loop on an app Clear site data for that URL; confirm the app is running NeutArr asks for a setup token Catalog → NeutArr → Settings after NeutArr is running. The token is removed once the NeutArr account exists Permission errors writing files Host folder owner must match the container user (PUID/PGID) Sonarr imports but duplicates files Downloads and media must share one filesystem for hardlinks Works at home, not on phone data Need Tunnel (+ ideally Access); LAN IPs are not reachable from mobile data Two Sonarrs fighting Remove any extra Sonarr container; only AIO should run it Server graph counts only this container Mount host /sys read-only at /host/sys and recreate (Docker) Jellyfin recently added looks short Scroll the rail — it loads further pages. If the rail stays empty, set a Jellyfin API key under Settings → Homepage Plex recently added stops at 20 That list is Plex's latest 20 qBittorrent / Prowlarr / Flaresolverr stay stopped after boot VPN is on without a live handshake. Check Settings → Network; AIO retries the tunnel and starts those apps when it is up. A manual VPN Stop cancels the retry Prowlarr indexers unavailable / RSS failures Often a DNS timeout through the VPN. After updating AIO, recreate the container, then Test All in Prowlarr (and re-test in Sonarr/Radarr) so the old failure backoff clears. A debug share shows VPN DNS cache hits and per-resolver failures cloudflared logs connection refused at boot Expected on older images when the tunnel started before apps. Current images start Cloudflare last; recreate from a current nightly / latest

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
Reach AIO (and optional apps like Sonarr or Jellyfin) from the internet without opening ports on your router.

How it works in plain terms: a small program (cloudflared) runs inside AIO, dials out to Cloudflare, and Cloudflare serves https://your-name.yourdomain.com. Your home firewall stays closed to inbound traffic.

Do not install a second Cloudflare Docker container or cloudflared service on the same host for the same tunnel — AIO already runs it.

Official Cloudflare help: Create a tunnel · Tunnel token.

Your LAN UI at http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080 still works when the tunnel is off.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A domain whose DNS is on Cloudflare
  • Permission to create tunnels (Networking → Tunnels)
  • AIO already installed and through first-run setup

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the tunnel
docs.text:
1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.
  2. Open Networking → Tunnels (some accounts still show Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels — same place).
  3. Create a tunnel → connector type Cloudflared.
  4. Name it clearly, e.g. aio-media-manager.
  5. Create Tunnel.

docs.title: Step 2 — Copy only the token
docs.text:
Cloudflare shows install commands for Docker, Windows, etc. Do not run those on your NAS. You only need the token string.

  1. Stay on the tunnel setup / Overview page.
  2. Pick any OS so a command appears (or later: tunnel → Overview → Add a replica).
  3. You will see something like:
cloudflared service install eyJhIjoiNWFiNGU5Z...very-long...
  1. Copy only the part that starts with eyJ (long JWT-style string). Treat it like a password — anyone with it can run your tunnel.

Lost the token? Tunnel → Overview → Add a replica → copy eyJ… again. Leaked? Use Refresh token, paste the new one into AIO, Save.

docs.title: Step 3 — Paste the connector token into AIO
docs.text:
1. Open http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080.
  2. Settings → Network → Cloudflare Tunnel
  3. Turn Enable tunnel on, paste the eyJ… token, Save.
  4. Status should show Enabled, Token saved, Tunnel up, cloudflared ready. The header CF pill turns green/blue when healthy.

On container boot, AIO brings up the VPN (if enabled) and the catalog apps first, then starts cloudflared last so it does not probe origins that are still starting. The dashboard is reachable while that is still happening. After the first-run wizard, the tunnel still starts as soon as you finish the wizard (before or with the VPN), so you can publish hostnames right away.

Stuck on Tunnel down? Check cloudflared logs in Catalog/Diagnostics, outbound access to Cloudflare (port 7844), and that nothing else is using the same token.

docs.title: Step 4 — Publish applications (so Open UI works remotely)
docs.text:
Cloudflare only serves HTTPS on port 443. You cannot open https://media.example.com:8989. Each app needs its own public hostname, e.g. https://sonarr.example.com, mapped to http://127.0.0.1:8989 inside the AIO container.

Jellyfin: the tunnel points at a localhost nginx on 8097 that copies CF-Connecting-IP into X-Forwarded-For before Jellyfin. Without that, Jellyfin sees every tunnel client as 127.0.0.1 (local) and skips remote bitrate / Auto transcode. LAN still uses 8096 directly.

In Cloudflare these are Published applications (hostname → service) — not private-network Tunnel CIDR routes.

docs.title: Easiest: do it in AIO
docs.text:
After the tunnel connector token is saved (Step 3):

  1. Settings → Network → Public subdomains
  2. Set Public app domain to your zone (e.g. example.com or example.co.uk).
  3. Create an API token the way Cloudflare documents (Create API token):
  4. My Profile → API Tokens (user) or Manage Account → Account API Tokens
  5. Create Token → start from the Edit zone DNS template
  6. Keep Zone → DNS → Edit, limited to your zone
  7. Add Account → Cloudflare Tunnel → Edit (and preferably Zone → Zone → Read)
  8. Continue to summary → Create Token (copy the secret once)
  9. Paste that API token under Public subdomains (this is not the eyJ… tunnel connector token from Step 3, and not the Global API Key). If Cloudflare returns Invalid access token, clear the saved token and paste a fresh API Token from Create Token.
  10. Toggle Expose per app, edit subdomain labels if you like, Save, then Publish to Cloudflare.

Save updates Catalog Open UI and Home widget links. Publish writes published applications into the tunnel and creates proxied DNS CNAMEs (<subdomain>.yourzone → <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com).

Typical service targets (inside AIO):

Hostname Points to (inside AIO) media.example.com (AIO) http://127.0.0.1:8080 qbittorrent.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8081 shelfmark.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8084 sabnzbd.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8085 jellyfin.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8097 (CF origin shim → Jellyfin :8096) seerr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:5055 grimmory.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6060 bazarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6767 nzbget.example.com http://127.0.0.1:6789 radarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:7878 lidarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8686 sonarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:8989 prowlarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:9696 neutarr.example.com http://127.0.0.1:9705 plex.example.com http://127.0.0.1:32400

Flaresolverr and Recyclarr are not offered as public hostnames. Recyclarr is a command-line sync. Flaresolverr is used inside the appliance by Prowlarr. More ports: Install → Ports.

docs.title: Or: publish by hand in Cloudflare
docs.text:
Networking → Tunnels → your tunnel → Routes → Published application. Service URL must be http://127.0.0.1:PORT inside AIO. Then match the same labels under AIO Public subdomains → Save so Open UI / Home links agree.

Publish behaviour

  • AIO only changes hostnames it published (or that you enable now). Hand-made dashboard hostnames you never published from AIO stay put.
  • Turning an app off and publishing again removes its ingress hostname; the DNS name may remain (then you get a tunnel 404).
  • Changing an app’s listen port updates the tunnel service when an API token is saved.
  • At home, http://nas-ip:8080 still opens apps as http://nas-ip:port even if a public domain is set.

Important: published hostnames are on the public internet until you add Cloudflare Access. Put Access in front of the *Arr apps, the download clients, and Seerr. Leave the AIO dashboard, Jellyfin, and Plex on their own login. AIO can create those Access applications after you add a login method in Zero Trust.

SABnzbd blocks unknown public Hosts by default (External internet access denied). AIO sets inet_exposure and adds your published SABnzbd hostname to host_whitelist on start / Auto-Wire / Publish. After enabling sabnzbd under Public subdomains, restart SABnzbd or run Auto-Wire once if the page still denies access.

docs.title: Optional: token file on disk (SSH / Compose)
docs.text:
Handy for env-driven installs. Paths are on the host side of /config:

Platform Folder for tunnel.token Generic Linux /opt/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/ Unraid /mnt/user/appdata/aio-media-manager/cloudflare/ Synology /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/ 
ssh user@host
CONFIG=/opt/aio-media-manager/config
sudo mkdir -p "$CONFIG/cloudflare"
sudo tee "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
eyJ...paste-token...
EOF
sudo chmod 600 "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token"
sudo chown "${PUID:-1000}:${PGID:-1000}" "$CONFIG/cloudflare/tunnel.token"

Then enable in Settings → Network (preferred — it is saved in amm_config.json and survives container restarts even if compose still has AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED=false), or set and recreate:

AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED=true
AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE=/config/cloudflare/tunnel.token

Keep a single AIO service in Compose — no separate cloudflare/cloudflared container.

docs.title: Native Linux (no Docker)
docs.text:
Install the cloudflared binary if you are not on the GHCR image, but do not run cloudflared service install — AIO starts the process:

sudo mkdir -p --mode=0755 /usr/share/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-main.gpg | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg >/dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/cloudflare-main.gpg] https://pkg.cloudflare.com/cloudflared any main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/cloudflared.list
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install cloudflared

Enable the tunnel in Settings (or env) and start aio-media-manager.service.

docs.title: Check that it works
docs.text:
1. Cloudflare: tunnel status Healthy
  2. AIO: Settings → Network → tunnel connected
  3. From mobile data (or another network): open https://media.example.com (your hostname)
  4. Optional API check (does not return the token): GET /api/cloudflare/tunnel/status

docs.title: Trusted reverse-proxy IPs
docs.text:
Settings → Network → Trusted reverse-proxy IPs (AMM_TRUSTED_PROXIES).

This tells AIO which nearby proxies may send X-Forwarded-* headers (real client IP and https vs http).

Your setup What to put LAN only Leave empty Cloudflare Tunnel only (token in AIO) Leave empty — AIO already trusts local cloudflared nginx / Caddy / Traefik in front of AIO That proxy’s IP (as AIO sees it), e.g. 172.17.0.1

This is not a list of Cloudflare’s public edge IPs. With a tunnel, traffic arrives from local cloudflared. Do not set * unless you understand spoofing risk. Restart the container after changing this field.

Access login gate: CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS.md — trusted proxies do not replace Access.

  2. Copy eyJ… — do not run Cloudflare’s installer on the NAS.

docs.title: Cloudflare Access (login gate)
docs.text:
Use both doors. Cloudflare Access is the extra login in front of the *Arr apps, the download clients, and Seerr. The AIO dashboard, Jellyfin, and Plex keep the login they already have.

Access does not replace Sonarr’s password or Seerr’s account. It only asks who you are before that page loads. Addresses on your home network (http://nas-ip:8989) skip Access. Calls inside AIO on 127.0.0.1 skip it too.

Publish the hostnames first: Cloudflare Tunnel.

Official Cloudflare docs: Self-hosted apps · Policies · Identity providers.

docs.title: Which hostname gets which login
docs.text:
Hostname (example) Login Why media.example.com (AIO) AIO’s own account Same idea as Jellyfin and Plex: one login you already set up jellyfin / plex That app’s own account Phone and TV apps cannot complete an Access page sonarr / radarr / lidarr / prowlarr / bazarr Cloudflare Access, then the app password Admin UIs. Browsers handle the Access page qbittorrent / sabnzbd / nzbget Cloudflare Access, then the app password Download clients, same as *Arr seerr Cloudflare Access, then Seerr’s own account Request UI in the browser

Shelfmark, Grimmory, and NeutArr stay on their own login unless you add an Access application for them yourself.

Do not put the AIO hostname, Jellyfin, or Plex on an Access application. A wildcard *.example.com would catch them too. AIO creates one application per protected hostname.

docs.title: 1. Open Zero Trust
docs.text:
1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com.
  2. Open Zero Trust. If this account has no Zero Trust organization yet, create one and pick a team name. The free plan is enough for a household. See Create a Zero Trust organization.

The team name is the <your-team-name> in the Google redirect URL below. Find it under Settings → Team name and domain.

docs.title: 2. Add the login method yourself
docs.text: Pick one. You can add another later. AIO does not create this for you.

docs.title: Cloudflare account (uses the MFA on that account)
docs.text:
New Zero Trust organizations already have the Cloudflare identity provider. People sign in with their Cloudflare account. Multi-factor authentication is the 2FA already on that Cloudflare user, not a separate switch inside Access.

  1. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers.
  2. If Cloudflare is missing: Add new identity provider → Cloudflare.
  3. Turn on Restrict to account members, then Save.

With that switch on, a stranger who merely owns some Cloudflare account cannot sign in. Add the people who should reach Sonarr as members of this Cloudflare account, and have them turn on 2FA on their Cloudflare user.

docs.title: Google
docs.text:
Follow Google. In short:

  1. In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client of type Web application.
  2. Authorized JavaScript origin:
https://<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com
  1. Authorized redirect URI:
https://<your-team-name>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/callback
  1. Copy the client ID and client secret.
  2. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers → Add new identity provider → Google. Paste both values and Save.
  3. Select Test next to Google.

A Google login by itself lets any Google account through. The Allow policy in the next section must list the addresses that may enter.

Google Workspace (groups from an organization) is a different provider: Google Workspace.

docs.title: One-time PIN
docs.text:
Use this when people should get a code by email and you do not want a Google or Cloudflare account. See One-time PIN.

  1. Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers → Add new identity provider → One-time PIN.
  2. The Allow policy must list those email addresses. A policy that only says “One-time PIN” lets anyone who can read a mailbox request a code.

docs.title: 3. Who is allowed in
docs.text:
Access denies everyone until an Allow policy matches.

Field Value Policy name Admins Action Allow Include Emails → the addresses that may open Sonarr and the download clients

If you use the Cloudflare identity provider with Restrict to account members, you can instead include Login methods → Cloudflare.

You do not need a separate Block rule. No match means deny.

docs.title: 4. Add Access from AIO
docs.text:
After the login method exists, AIO creates the Access applications. It does not create the login method.

  1. Settings → Network → Public subdomains.
  2. Turn on Expose for the *Arr apps, download clients, and Seerr you want on the internet. Leave Jellyfin, Plex, and AIO off Access (they are marked Own login).
  3. Publish to Cloudflare first, so the hostnames exist.
  4. Under Cloudflare Access emails, list the addresses that may enter. Leave the list empty only when the only login method is Cloudflare with Restrict to account members.
  5. Add Cloudflare Access.

The API token needs two extra permissions, on top of zone DNS Edit and Cloudflare Tunnel Edit:

  • Access: Apps and Policies → Write
  • Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups → Read

AIO writes one Allow policy named AIO Access and one self-hosted application per exposed protected hostname. Session length is 8 hours for *Arr and download clients, and 24 hours for Seerr. Running the button again updates those applications. Turning Expose off and running it again deletes only the Access applications AIO created.

To do the same by hand: Access controls → Applications → Create → Self-hosted, one hostname at a time, attach the Allow policy, and skip media, jellyfin, and plex.

docs.title: 5. Test it
docs.text:
1. Open a private window.
  2. Visit https://sonarr.example.com. You should see Cloudflare Access first, then Sonarr’s own login.
  3. Visit https://seerr.example.com. You should see Cloudflare Access first, then Seerr.
  4. Visit https://jellyfin.example.com and https://media.example.com. You should see Jellyfin’s login and AIO’s login, with no Access page in front.
  5. From home wifi, http://nas-ip:8989 still opens Sonarr without Access. Use that only at home.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check No Access login on Sonarr That hostname is missing from Access, or a typo Access login on Jellyfin, Plex, or AIO Remove that hostname from the Access application. A * wildcard causes this Login loop Overlapping Access apps, or Google Workspace protecting a Google-hosted page. Try one app 403 after login The Allow policy does not match this email or Cloudflare account Any Google account can enter The policy includes the Google login method and does not list emails *Arr inside AIO stops talking to each other It should not. Browser Access does not affect calls on 127.0.0.1

docs.title: Quick checklistDonate
docs.text:
1. Tunnel up and hostnames published (Tunnel guide).
  2. Add a login method: Cloudflare account, Google, or One-time PIN.
  3. Allow policy limited to your admin emails, or to members of this Cloudflare account.
  4. Add Cloudflare Access in AIO for each exposed *Arr app, download client, and Seerr.
  5. Leave AIO, Jellyfin, and Plex on their own login.
  6. Test Sonarr and Seerr in a private window, then test Jellyfin and the AIO dashboard.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
This is the usual way to run AIO: one container that starts the manager and every app you enable.

Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest Works on: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (On ARM, Flaresolverr is not available — it needs x86_64.)

docs.title: 1. Create folders (over SSH)
docs.text:
ssh user@host

id
export PUID="$(id -u)"
export PGID="$(id -g)"
export AMM_DATA_HOST="${HOME}/aio-media-manager"

mkdir -p "${AMM_DATA_HOST}/downloads" "${AMM_DATA_HOST}/media"
sudo mkdir -p /opt/aio-media-manager/{config,config/vpn,backups}
sudo chown -R "${PUID}:${PGID}" "${AMM_DATA_HOST}" /opt/aio-media-manager

Why these paths?

  • Downloads and media live under your home so the host file manager can see them.
  • Keep them as two folders under one parent so hardlinks work. Separate mounts on different disks (or different btrfs subvolumes) often force full copies.
  • Put backups on another disk than config when you can. Without a /backups mount, AIO falls back to /config/backups and warns in Settings.

Already have libraries elsewhere? Set AMM_DATA_HOST to that parent folder (it still needs downloads and media inside it).

docs.title: 2. Start with Compose (recommended)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager.git
cd aio-media-server-manager

Check docker-compose.yml:

  • Volume paths match the folders you created
  • PUID / PGID match id
  • TZ is your timezone (or set it later in Settings)

If you use sudo docker compose, set AMM_DATA_HOST explicitly so data does not land in /root.

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Open http://YOUR-HOST:8080, create the admin account, then follow Using the dashboard.

Updating later: pull again, then recreate:

docker compose pull
docker compose up -d --force-recreate

The container cannot replace its own image. Settings → Updates notifies a :nightly install only when :nightly moves, and a :latest install only when :latest moves. You still pull that tag on the host. Installed apps (Sonarr, Seerr, and the rest) update from Settings → Updates, one at a time or all at once. Those schedules default to off. Recreating the container does not bump them.

Older compose that only published port 8080? Copy the current ports: list from this repo and recreate, or child Open UI links will fail on the LAN.

Adding /backups later: create the host folder, add - /path/to/backups:/backups under volumes:, recreate. Old backups under /config/backups stay restorable until you remove them.

Host network traffic on Home: add - /sys:/host/sys:ro under volumes: and recreate. Without it, Home shows only the container's own traffic.

Optional GITHUB_TOKEN (compose or Settings → Updates) raises GitHub API limits. Do not commit the token.

docs.title: Build from this checkout
docs.text: docker compose up -d --build

docs.title: Dev / test environment
docs.text:
./scripts/test-env.sh up

See CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Hardware transcoding (Intel/AMD)
docs.text:
The image includes jellyfin-ffmpeg (with Intel iHD / VA-API drivers). Map the host render node, recreate the container after pulling a build that has it, then in Jellyfin enable Intel Quick Sync (or VAAPI) under Playback → Transcoding.

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f compose.gpu.yml up -d

docs.title: 3. Plain docker run (alternative)
docs.text:
docker pull ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest

docker run -d --name aio-media-manager --restart unless-stopped \
  --privileged \
  --cap-add NET_ADMIN --cap-add SYS_MODULE \
  --device /dev/dri:/dev/dri \
  -p 8080:8080 \
  -p 8081:8081 -p 8084:8084 -p 8085:8085 -p 8096:8096 \
  -p 8191:8191 -p 5055:5055 -p 6060:6060 \
  -p 6767:6767 -p 6789:6789 \
  -p 7878:7878 -p 8686:8686 -p 8989:8989 -p 9696:9696 -p 9705:9705 \
  -p 32400:32400 \
  -e PUID="${PUID}" -e PGID="${PGID}" \
  -e TZ=UTC \
  -v /opt/aio-media-manager/config:/config \
  -v "${HOME}/aio-media-manager:/data" \
  -v /opt/aio-media-manager/backups:/backups \
  -v /sys:/host/sys:ro \
  -e AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR=/data/downloads \
  -e AMM_MEDIA_DIR=/data/media \
  ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest

Drop --device /dev/dri if the host has no Intel/AMD GPU (Docker Desktop on a Mac, many VPS hosts). Or use --network host instead of listing every -p.

Full port list: Install → Ports.

docs.title: Private GHCR image
docs.text:
If pull fails because the package is private:

echo "$GITHUB_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME --password-stdin
docker pull ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest

On GitHub you can also make the package public under Packages → settings → Change visibility.

docs.title: Optional VPN
docs.text:
For qBittorrent / Prowlarr / Flaresolverr traffic:

sudo mkdir -p /opt/aio-media-manager/config/vpn
sudo chown -R "${PUID}:${PGID}" /opt/aio-media-manager/config/vpn
# copy wg0.conf or an OpenVPN profile into that folder
  1. Set AMM_VPN_ENABLED=true (and AMM_VPN_ENFORCE=true if torrents must not run without VPN).
  2. Leave Usenet clients off the VPN — they use the normal network.
  3. Save the profile under Settings → Network (or mount it and enable via env), then recreate the container so WireGuard comes up on boot.

Privileged mode is required for /dev/net/tun and the VPN uid routing (WireGuard in the main network namespace; torrent apps run as a dedicated uid). Synology often needs wireguard-go from the image when the host has no WireGuard kernel module — see SYNOLOGY.md.

docs.title: What AIO does while VPN is on
docs.text:
• Those three apps start only after a live WireGuard handshake. If the tunnel is down at boot, they wait; AIO retries the VPN with backoff and starts them when it is up. A manual VPN Stop cancels that retry.
  • DNS for those apps goes through a small caching forwarder inside AIO (127.0.0.153), bound to the tunnel interface so lookups cannot leak onto the house WAN. It asks several public resolvers in parallel and can serve a recent answer when upstream is briefly quiet — which keeps Prowlarr indexers from failing on a single timeout. Other apps (Sonarr, Radarr, SABnzbd, …) keep the container resolver.
  • Usenet traffic never uses the tunnel.

docs.title: Reverse proxy or CloudflareDonate
docs.text:
• No proxy needed for home LAN use at http://server-ip:8080.
  • Your own Traefik/Caddy/Nginx: set AMM_TRUSTED_PROXIES and optionally AMM_ROOT_PATH.
  • Cloudflare Tunnel (no inbound ports): CLOUDFLARE.md. cloudflared runs inside this container — do not add a second Cloudflare service.

docs.title: Linux / LXC (no Docker)
docs.text: Use this on Debian, Ubuntu, or a Proxmox LXC when you prefer not to use Docker. Sonarr and the rest still run as processes under AIO — you do not create a systemd unit per app.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Python 3.11+
  • Poetry
  • Node.js 22 (build the dashboard once)
  • ffmpeg (for transcoding / some media apps); for Jellyfin HW use jellyfin-ffmpeg7 from repo.jellyfin.org when possible
  • Optional VPN: wireguard or openvpn, plus iproute2 On LXC: enable nesting=1 and /dev/net/tun

docs.title: Create folders over SSH
docs.text:
ssh user@host

LOGIN_USER="${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"
HOME_DIR="$(getent passwd "${LOGIN_USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"
DATA="${HOME_DIR}/aio-media-manager"

sudo useradd --system --create-home --home-dir /opt/aio-media-manager --shell /usr/sbin/nologin amm || true
sudo mkdir -p \
  /opt/aio-media-manager \
  /var/lib/aio-media-manager/config \
  /var/lib/aio-media-manager/config/vpn \
  /var/lib/aio-media-manager/backups \
  "${DATA}/downloads" \
  "${DATA}/media"
sudo chown -R amm:amm /opt/aio-media-manager /var/lib/aio-media-manager "${DATA}"
id amm

Downloads and media stay in the login user's home (~/aio-media-manager) so the desktop file manager can see them. Config stays under /var/lib. To use existing library paths, keep downloads and media as siblings on the same filesystem and point .env at those directories.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
sudo -u amm git clone https://github.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager.git /opt/aio-media-manager
cd /opt/aio-media-manager
sudo -u amm cp .env.example .env

LOGIN_USER="${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"
HOME_DIR="$(getent passwd "${LOGIN_USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"
DATA="${HOME_DIR}/aio-media-manager"
sudo sed -i \
  -e "s|^AMM_CONFIG_DIR=.*|AMM_CONFIG_DIR=/var/lib/aio-media-manager/config|" \
  -e "s|^AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR=.*|AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR=${DATA}/downloads|" \
  -e "s|^AMM_MEDIA_DIR=.*|AMM_MEDIA_DIR=${DATA}/media|" \
  -e "s|^# AMM_BACKUP_DIR=.*|AMM_BACKUP_DIR=/var/lib/aio-media-manager/backups|" \
  /opt/aio-media-manager/.env

Point AMM_CONFIG_DIR, AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR, AMM_MEDIA_DIR, and AMM_BACKUP_DIR in .env at the directories you created (~/aio-media-manager/downloads and ~/aio-media-manager/media by default). Put AMM_BACKUP_DIR on another disk or mount if you can. Set PUID/PGID to id amm (or your media user). Set TZ (or AMM_TIMEZONE) to your IANA timezone. Optional GITHUB_TOKEN and update-schedule variables are documented in .env.example; you can also set them in Settings after first-run.

sudo -u amm poetry install --only main --no-interaction
sudo -u amm bash -lc 'cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build'

sudo cp deploy/aio-media-manager.service /etc/systemd/system/
LOGIN_USER="${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"
HOME_DIR="$(getent passwd "${LOGIN_USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"
sudo sed -i "s|/home/YOURUSER|${HOME_DIR}|g" /etc/systemd/system/aio-media-manager.service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now aio-media-manager

Open http://<host>:8080. Installed apps update later from Settings → Updates (schedules default to off). Updating this checkout and restarting the service updates AIO itself. On a native install, Home's Server card already sees the host's network cards.

If systemd-managed Python is 3.14+, install a 3.13 interpreter for Bazarr (AMM_CHILD_PYTHON pointing at python3.13) or Bazarr will fail on missing PIL / unsupported Python.

docs.title: Host packages by application
docs.text:
Install only what you will run. On ARM64, skip Chromium — Flaresolverr is x86_64-only and is hidden from the catalog.

Packages Applications jellyfin-ffmpeg7 (preferred) or ffmpeg, libfontconfig1 Jellyfin, Plex libicu*, libssl3, libsqlite3-0, sqlite3, libgssapi-krb5-2, zlib1g Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, NeutArr git Recyclarr (clones TRaSH Guides) unrar (RAR 5+), p7zip-full, par2cmdline-turbo as par2 SABnzbd, NZBGet Python 3.13, libxml2, libxslt1.1, libjpeg62-turbo, python3-dev, build-essential Bazarr, SABnzbd, NeutArr Manager Python 3.14, python3-dev, build-essential Shelfmark (upstream requires Python >= 3.14) Node.js 22 Seerr JRE 25, mariadb-server Grimmory chromium, xvfb, fonts-liberation Flaresolverr (x86_64 only) iproute2, openvpn, wireguard-tools Optional VPN (qBittorrent, Prowlarr, Flaresolverr)

docs.title: Service file
docs.text: aio-media-manager.service starts /opt/aio-media-manager/.venv/bin/python main.py. If Poetry placed the venv elsewhere, update ExecStart (poetry env info -p). The unit’s download/media paths must match the login home (sed in the install steps above).

docs.title: LXC notesDonate
docs.text:
• Unprivileged containers cannot create VPN network namespaces; skip VPN or use a privileged CT.
  • Bind-mount media into the CT under the login home (~/aio-media-manager); keep downloads and media on the same dataset for hardlinks.

docs.title: Synology
docs.text:
Run AIO as one Container Manager project. Do not add extra services or separate Sonarr/Radarr/download containers next to it.

Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest Your DSM needs to run linux/amd64 or linux/arm64 images.

docs.title: Create folders and the project (SSH)
docs.text:
Enable SSH (Control Panel → Terminal & SNMP → Enable SSH service), then:

ssh admin@<nas-ip>

The install script creates /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager (with config/ and backups/) and a data tree in the DSM user home (File Station → Home → aio-media-manager with downloads/ and media/). That path is a real user home, so DSM can browse it. A raw /volume1/data folder is not a shared folder and does not show up in File Station; re-running the script moves that tree into home if it still exists. Downloads and media stay one bind (/data) so *Arr can hardlink. Config backups go to the /backups mount; include that folder in a Hyper Backup task, or point BACKUPS= at another volume.

User Home Service must be on (Control Panel → User & Group → Advanced). SSH as the DSM user whose Home should hold the libraries, or set HOME_USER=.

id
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager/main/deploy/synology/install.sh | sudo sh

If SSH is admin but Home should belong to another DSM user:

id media
sudo HOME_USER=media PUID=1026 PGID=100 sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager/main/deploy/synology/install.sh | sh'

Other volume or paths:

sudo VOLUME=/volume2 \
     HOME_USER=media \
     BACKUPS=/volume1/backups/aio-media-manager \
     PUID=1026 PGID=100 \
     sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager/main/deploy/synology/install.sh | sh'

To keep libraries on a DSM shared folder instead of Home, set DATA= to that folder (still one parent for downloads and media):

sudo DATA=/volume1/media/aio-media-manager \
     PUID=1026 PGID=100 \
     sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager/main/deploy/synology/install.sh | sh'

The generated file is /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/docker-compose.yml (no build: key — Container Manager pulls GHCR). A static copy lives in synology/docker-compose.yml.

If GHCR is private: sudo docker login ghcr.io before starting the project.

docs.title: Import in Container Manager
docs.text:
1. Open Container Manager → Project → Create.
  2. Project name: aio-media-manager
  3. Path: /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager (same folder the script used).
  4. Source: use the existing docker-compose.yml (do not paste a second compose file or add more services).
  5. Start the project.

The UI should show a single service aio-media-manager. Open http://<nas-ip>:8080 for the manager. Open UI on catalog cards uses the app ports (Sonarr 8989, Radarr 7878, …), which the project compose now publishes. If you generated compose before that change, copy the ports: list from synology/docker-compose.yml into the project file and recreate the container.

The install script also mounts host /sys read-only at /host/sys so Home's Server card shows the NAS network traffic. If the project compose was generated before that, add - /sys:/host/sys:ro under volumes: and recreate. Without it, the graph is only this container's traffic. Installed apps update later from Settings → Updates (schedules default to off). Recreating the project updates AIO.

To start from SSH instead of the UI:

sudo docker compose -f /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/docker-compose.yml pull
sudo docker compose -f /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/docker-compose.yml up -d

After that, Container Manager still lists it if the project path matches.

docs.title: Hardware transcoding
docs.text:
If /dev/dri exists, add this block under aio-media-manager in the project compose file, then recreate and start the project:

    devices:
      - /dev/dri:/dev/dri

ls -l /dev/dri

docs.title: VPN (qBittorrent, Prowlarr, Flaresolverr)
docs.text:
sudo mkdir -p /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/vpn
# scp wg0.conf into that directory

Set AMM_VPN_ENABLED=true in the project compose, then start the project again. While VPN is on, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, and Flaresolverr cannot use the house WAN: they only leave through the tunnel. If the tunnel is down at boot, they wait; AIO retries the VPN and starts them when the handshake is back. A local DNS cache for those apps (bound to the tunnel) reduces indexer failures from short DNS timeouts. Synology’s kernel often has no WireGuard module; the appliance image includes wireguard-go as a fallback and creates /dev/net/tun when it is missing. That only works if the project stays privileged: true (the install script sets this). Recreate the container after pulling a current image, then save VPN in Settings → Network. OpenVPN uses the same device node and also needs privileged mode. On DSM, Synology ACL can block the VPN app uid (910) after chown; if those apps cannot write their config folders, clear the ACL on the host path as the logs describe.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
Do not add a second project service. Write the token on the NAS, then enable the tunnel in Settings → Network (saved across restarts). Optionally set AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_ENABLED=true in the project compose. See CLOUDFLARE.md.

sudo mkdir -p /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare
sudo tee /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/tunnel.token >/dev/null <<'EOF'
eyJ...paste-token...
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /volume1/docker/aio-media-manager/config/cloudflare/tunnel.token

docs.text:
Deploy AIO as one custom app / Docker install. Do not also install Sonarr, Radarr, or download clients as separate SCALE apps if you want this all-in-one model.

Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest

docs.title: Create datasets and folders (SSH)
docs.text:
Enable SSH (System → Services → SSH), then:

ssh admin@<truenas-ip>

Replace tank with your pool name. Config stays on an apps dataset. Downloads and media go in the login user's home so the Files UI can browse them (~/aio-media-manager). Keep those two as directories on the same dataset so *Arr can hardlink.

sudo zfs create -p tank/apps/aio-media-manager
sudo zfs create -p tank/backups/aio-media-manager

LOGIN_USER="${SUDO_USER:-$(id -un)}"
HOME_DIR="$(getent passwd "${LOGIN_USER}" | cut -d: -f6)"
DATA="${HOME_DIR}/aio-media-manager"

sudo mkdir -p \
  /mnt/tank/apps/aio-media-manager/vpn \
  "${DATA}/downloads" \
  "${DATA}/media"

tank/backups/aio-media-manager holds configuration backups. A separate dataset lets you snapshot or replicate it on its own schedule. Put it on another pool if you have one.

TV, movies, anime, music, books, comics, complete/incomplete downloads, torrent category folders, and transcode caches are created inside these mounts on first start.

Set the owner to your media user (TrueNAS apps is often UID/GID 568; confirm with id apps or id):

id apps
sudo chown -R 568:568 \
  /mnt/tank/apps/aio-media-manager \
  "${DATA}" \
  /mnt/tank/backups/aio-media-manager

If user home is not enabled, create it under Credentials → Users, or set DATA to a folder you can see in Files (still one parent for downloads and media).

docs.title: Custom App
docs.text:
1. Apps → Discover → Custom App (or Launch Docker Image).
  2. Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest
  3. Port forwarding: 8080 → 8080 plus the child WebUI ports from INSTALL.md (or host network).
  4. Storage (paths from the SSH commands above):
  5. /mnt/tank/apps/aio-media-manager → /config
  6. $HOME/aio-media-manager → /data
  7. /mnt/tank/backups/aio-media-manager → /backups
  8. /sys → /host/sys (read-only), so Home's Server card shows the server's network traffic. Without it, the graph is only this container's traffic.
  9. Environment: PUID / PGID = the UID/GID you used with chown, plus TZ, AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR=/data/downloads and AMM_MEDIA_DIR=/data/media. Optional GITHUB_TOKEN for GitHub rate limits (or Settings → Updates after first-run).
  10. Privileged / NET_ADMIN if you enable VPN for qBittorrent, Prowlarr, and Flaresolverr. Those apps wait for a live tunnel; DNS for them is cached through the tunnel (Usenet stays off it). Details: DOCKER.md.
  11. GPU: pass /dev/dri (Intel/AMD) or NVIDIA runtime when transcoding.

The manager UI is http://<truenas-ip>:8080. Recreate the custom app after an image update so newly published ports apply.

docs.title: Unraid
docs.text:
Install one AIO container. Do not also add Community Applications templates for Sonarr, Radarr, or download clients — AIO runs those inside itself.

Templates in this repo

File Purpose unraid/templates/aio-media-manager.xml Docker template (ports, paths, env) unraid/ca_profile.xml Community Applications maintainer profile unraid.xml Older path for the same template (compatibility)

docs.title: Create folders over SSH
docs.text:
Enable SSH (Settings → Management Access), then:

ssh root@<unraid-ip>

Downloads and media live on the user share aio-media-manager (visible in Shares / the file browser). Config stays in appdata.

mkdir -p \
  /mnt/user/appdata/aio-media-manager/vpn \
  /mnt/user/backups/aio-media-manager \
  /mnt/user/aio-media-manager/downloads \
  /mnt/user/aio-media-manager/media

chown -R 99:100 \
  /mnt/user/appdata/aio-media-manager \
  /mnt/user/backups/aio-media-manager \
  /mnt/user/aio-media-manager

/mnt/user/backups/aio-media-manager receives the configuration backups. Use a share that lives on the array (not only the cache pool), so a cache failure does not take the backups with it.

TV, movies, anime, music, books, comics, complete/incomplete downloads, torrent category folders, and transcode caches are created inside these mounts on first start.

99:100 is Unraid nobody/users (PUID 99, PGID 100). If you use a custom share user, run id thatuser and chown to that UID:GID instead.

For hardlinks, keep downloads and media as subfolders of one cache or disk path (not two /mnt/user FUSE shares), for example a cache-only share named aio-media-manager:

mkdir -p /mnt/cache/aio-media-manager/downloads /mnt/cache/aio-media-manager/media
chown -R 99:100 /mnt/cache/aio-media-manager

Then bind /data to /mnt/cache/aio-media-manager (same share, disk path) instead of /mnt/user/aio-media-manager.

docs.title: Option A — Local user template
docs.text:
1. Copy the XML onto the flash drive:
mkdir -p /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user
curl -fsSL \
  -o /boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/templates-user/my-aio-media-manager.xml \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Qballjos/aio-media-server-manager/main/deploy/unraid/templates/aio-media-manager.xml
  1. Docker → Add Container → select aio-media-manager (or my-aio-media-manager) from the Template list.
  2. Confirm paths, PUID/PGID, and TZ, then Apply.
  3. Open http://<unraid-ip>:8080 and run the wizard.

docs.title: Option B — Manual Add Container
docs.text:
1. Docker → Add Container → advanced view.
  2. Repository: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest
  3. Network: bridge (or host if you want every app WebUI on the Unraid IP).
  4. Privileged: On (needed for qBittorrent / Prowlarr / Flaresolverr VPN isolation). With VPN on, those apps wait for a live WireGuard handshake; AIO caches their DNS through the tunnel so short hiccups do not knock Prowlarr indexers offline. Details: DOCKER.md.
  5. Extra parameters: --cap-add=NET_ADMIN --cap-add=SYS_MODULE
  6. Optional device: /dev/dri for Intel/AMD transcoding (skip if missing).
  7. Ports (TCP): publish 8080 for the manager and the child WebUIs you installed (Sonarr 8989, Radarr 7878, qBittorrent 8081, SABnzbd 8085, Jellyfin 8096, Prowlarr 9696, Seerr 5055, Plex 32400, …). Full list: INSTALL.md. Or use Network host.
  8. Paths:
  9. /config → /mnt/user/appdata/aio-media-manager
  10. /data → /mnt/user/aio-media-manager
  11. /backups → /mnt/user/backups/aio-media-manager
  12. /host/sys → /sys (read-only). Home's Server card then shows the server's network traffic. The template lists this as Host sys (advanced). Without it, the graph is only this container's traffic.
  13. Variables: PUID=99, PGID=100, TZ=<IANA timezone>, AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR=/data/downloads, AMM_MEDIA_DIR=/data/media. Optional: GITHUB_TOKEN.

After updating the image, recreate the container so added WebUI port mappings take effect.

docs.title: Publish to Community Applications (public store)
docs.text: Community Apps does not host your files. You keep a public GitHub repo with templates; Lime Technology’s CA scanner indexes it after you submit.

docs.title: 1. Prepare a templates repository
docs.text:
Recommended: a dedicated public repo (for example Qballjos/unraid-templates) whose root looks like:

ca_profile.xml
templates/aio-media-manager.xml

Copy from this project:

# from a clone of aio-media-server-manager
mkdir -p ../unraid-templates/templates
cp deploy/unraid/ca_profile.xml ../unraid-templates/
cp deploy/unraid/templates/aio-media-manager.xml ../unraid-templates/templates/

Then:

  1. Create the public GitHub repo and push main.
  2. Edit templates/aio-media-manager.xml and set <TemplateURL> to the raw URL of that file in the new repo (must match the real path on main).
  3. Keep <Repository> as ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest (image stays on GHCR; only the template XML lives in the templates repo).
  4. Optional: open an Unraid forum support thread and put its URL in ca_profile.xml <Forum> and the template <Support> tags (GitHub Issues is fine to start).

You can submit the main app repo instead if the XML is discoverable and every app has a <Repository> tag, but a small dedicated templates repo is what CA maintainers usually expect.

docs.title: 2. Submit
docs.text:
1. Sign in at https://ca.unraid.net/submit with your Unraid / forum account.
  2. Register the GitHub repository URL (the templates repo).
  3. Run Validate, then Scan. Fix any reported XML issues.
  4. Wait for moderation. When approved, the app appears under the Apps tab for everyone.

Helpful docs:

  • Submission help
  • Repository XML format
  • XML field reference
  • Browse catalog (check for name clashes first)

Do not use the retired selfhosters/unRAID-CA-templates request flow.

docs.title: 3. After it is listed
docs.text:
• Ship updates by publishing a new container image (:latest or semver tags). Users update via Unraid’s Docker update — you usually do not bump the template for every release.
  • Change the template XML only when ports, paths, or env vars change; CA re-reads <TemplateURL> on refresh.

docs.title: Private / self-only (not the public store)
docs.text:
To use your own GitHub templates without CA approval, append the repo URL to:

/boot/config/plugins/dockerMan/template-repos

(one URL per line). Templates then appear under Docker → Add Container. That does not list the app in the public Community Applications catalog.

docs.title: FUSE / hardlinks
docs.text: Prefer /mnt/cache/aio-media-manager or a single disk path for downloads and media when you care about hardlinks. Mixing /mnt/user (FUSE) with a disk share can break atomic moves.

docs.title: UpdatesDonate
docs.text:
Change the repository tag or use Unraid's container update, then recreate so new ports and the Host sys mount apply. Images are published from main as :latest and from git tags as semver. That updates AIO. Installed apps update from Settings → Updates (schedules default to off).

docs.text:
Zet AIO in drie stappen aan: mappen maken, de app starten, het dashboard openen.

Liever een korte route?

De meeste mensen beginnen met Docker of hun NAS-gids (Unraid · Synology · TrueNAS) en komen daarna hier terug voor poorten en updates.

docs.title: Voordat je begint
docs.text:
1. Kies waar het draait — Unraid, Synology, TrueNAS, gewone Docker of native Linux.
  2. Plan twee soorten opslag:
  3. Config — instellingen en databases (klein, maak hier een back-up van)
  4. Downloads + media — de grote bestanden (houd die op dezelfde schijf/share, zodat hardlinks werken)
  5. Ken je gebruikers-ID — op Linux/NAS draaien apps vaak als een bepaalde gebruiker (PUID / PGID). Laat dat overeenkomen met de eigenaar van je mappen, anders krijg je rechtenfouten.

Je hebt maar één AIO-container nodig. Installeer Sonarr, Radarr of downloadclients niet als losse apps ernaast.

Image: ghcr.io/qballjos/aio-media-server-manager:latest Architecturen: linux/amd64, linux/arm64 (Flaresolverr is alleen x86_64 en verborgen op ARM)

docs.title: Kies je platform
docs.text:
Waar het draait Gids Docker (elke host) Docker Unraid Unraid Synology Synology TrueNAS SCALE TrueNAS Debian / Ubuntu / Proxmox LXC (geen Docker) Linux Alle opties op een rij Overzicht

Elke platformgids begint met: SSH openen → mappen maken → AIO starten.

docs.title: Mappen op de host
docs.text:
Log in via SSH en maak iets als dit (paden verschillen per platform — volg je gids):

ssh user@host

mkdir -p "$HOME/aio-media-manager/downloads" "$HOME/aio-media-manager/media"
sudo mkdir -p /path/to/config /path/to/config/vpn /path/to/backups
id   # note uid= (PUID) and gid= (PGID)
sudo chown -R "$PUID:$PGID" "$HOME/aio-media-manager" /path/to/config /path/to/backups

Houd downloads en media als buren onder één map, zodat *Arr kan hardlinken. Mount een aparte map backups op /backups als dat kan (bij voorkeur een andere schijf dan config).

In die mounts legt AIO bibliotheken aan zoals media/tv, media/movies en downloads/complete.

docs.title: Nadat het start
docs.text:
1. Open het dashboard: http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080 (Gebruik een andere poort als je die hebt gemapt.)
  2. Maak het beheerdersaccount (gebruikersnaam, e-mail, wachtwoord).
  3. Rond de wizard van de eerste start af en volg daarna Het dashboard gebruiken.

Na docker compose pull moet je de container opnieuw aanmaken (niet alleen herstarten), zodat nieuwe poorten en runtimes gelden. Dat werkt AIO bij. Geïnstalleerde apps werk je bij via Instellingen → Updates in het dashboard. Die schema’s staan standaard uit.

Het compose-bestand van de repo mount host-/sys alleen-lezen op /host/sys, zodat de serverkaart op Start de netwerkkaarten van de server telt. Een ouder compose-bestand zonder die regel toont alleen het verkeer van de container, tot je de regel toevoegt en opnieuw aanmaakt. Zie Docker.

1. Cloudflare Tunnel — HTTPS zonder routerpoorten open te zetten
  2. Cloudflare Access — een aanmeldpoort, zodat vreemden de beheerapps niet kunnen openen

docs.title: Poorten
docs.text:
De interface van de manager gebruikt 8080. Kind-apps luisteren in dezelfde container. Compose en NAS-sjablonen publiceren die poorten op de host, zodat Interface openen werkt (http://YOUR-IP:8989 voor Sonarr, enzovoort). Host-netwerk is een alternatief als je niet elke poort wilt mappen.

Applicatie Standaardpoort Manager-UI 8080 qBittorrent 8081 Shelfmark 8084 SABnzbd 8085 Jellyfin 8096 Flaresolverr 8191 (alleen x86_64) Bazarr 6767 NZBGet 6789 Lidarr 8686 Sonarr 8989 Radarr 7878 Prowlarr 9696 Seerr 5055 Grimmory 6060 NeutArr 9705 Recyclarr geen (alleen CLI) Plex 32400

Variabele Doel PUID / PGID Gebruiker waaronder de apps draaien (gelijk aan de mapeigenaar) TZ / AMM_TIMEZONE Tijdzone voor logs en schema’s AMM_DOWNLOAD_DIR / AMM_MEDIA_DIR Paden in de container (host-mounts wijzig je in compose) GITHUB_TOKEN Optioneel; hogere GitHub-API-limiet voor updates AMM_CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_* Optionele tunnel voor toegang van buitenaf (cloudflared start na de apps bij boot) AMM_VPN_* Optionele VPN voor qBittorrent, Prowlarr en Flaresolverr (ze wachten op de tunnel; lokale DNS-cache voor die apps)

Doel

Standaardadres op je thuisnetwerk:

http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8080

docs.title: Eerste keer
docs.text:
1. Maak het beheerdersaccount wanneer daarom wordt gevraagd (gebruikersnaam, e-mail, wachtwoord).
  2. Rond de wizard van de eerste start af: de apps die je wilt, een Usenet-server als je die gebruikt, optioneel VPN en een optionele Cloudflare Tunnel. De wizard installeert die keuze. De tunnel en de VPN starten meteen als de wizard klaar is, als je ze hebt aangezet.
  3. Na het opnieuw aanmaken van de container antwoordt het dashboard terwijl apps nog starten. Met VPN aan wachten qBittorrent, Prowlarr en Flaresolverr tot de WireGuard-handshake klaar is (AIO probeert de VPN opnieuw als de eerste poging mislukt). Cloudflare Tunnel start als laatste, nadat de apps antwoorden, zodat cloudflared geen connection refused logt tegen origins die nog niet luisteren.
  4. Wacht tot Catalogus die apps als actief toont. Gebruik Interface openen voor alles wat nog een eigen account heeft (Plex, Jellyfin, NZBGet).
  5. Voeg later meer toe vanuit Catalogus. Je hebt niet elke app nodig.

Begin klein (bijvoorbeeld Radarr + één downloadclient + Jellyfin) en voeg de rest daarna toe.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
Start is een raster. Telefoon, tablet en desktop houden elk hun eigen indeling (4, 8 en 12 kolommen). De indelingsknop op het tabblad Start verplaatst, vergroot, voegt toe en verwijdert widgets. Instellingen → Startpagina toont of verbergt de app-balk, zet de aanmeldtekst en bewaart een Jellyfin- of Seerr-API-sleutel als Start die zelf niet kan lezen.

Widget Wat hij toont Begroeting Moment van de dag Zoeken Zoeken in Seerr Kalender Aankomende afleveringen en films. Een seizoen dat op één dag valt, is één regel Downloaden Actieve downloads, met alles pauzeren / alles hervatten. Vastgelopen items kun je verwijderen Recent toegevoegd Nieuwe series en films. Scrollen laadt verdere Jellyfin-pagina’s. Plex blijft bij de laatste 20 Aanvragen Seerr-aanvragen die nog niet klaar zijn, plus wat de laatste 30 dagen als beschikbaar of afgewezen is gemarkeerd Trending De trendinglijst van Seerr. Scrollen blijft laden Wordt afgespeeld Wie kijkt op Jellyfin of Plex, inclusief direct afspelen Opslag Schijfgebruik van config, downloads en media Server CPU, geheugen en netwerk. Met host-/sys gemount op /host/sys zijn dit de netwerkkaarten van de server. Zonder die mount is het alleen het verkeer van deze container Aandacht nodig Dezelfde controles als Instellingen → Meldingen, met een link om elk punt op te lossen Overige downloads Standaard uit; voeg het toe via de indelingsknop. Wat SABnzbd, NZBGet en qBittorrent hebben gedownload dat geen film of serie is (muziek, boeken, games, software, archieven), elk met een icoon voor de soort

Installeren, starten, stoppen en Interface openen staan in Catalogus. De balk onderaan Start opent apps die al geïnstalleerd zijn.

Interface openen op het LAN ziet er meestal uit als http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8989 (voorbeeld voor Sonarr). Als je publieke Cloudflare-hostnamen hebt ingesteld, kan Interface openen in plaats daarvan https://sonarr.yourdomain.com gebruiken — zie Cloudflare Tunnel.

docs.title: Wat de wizard koppelt
docs.text:
Als een app gezond is — of als je op Auto-koppelen klikt — zet AIO downloadmappen en categorieën, hoofdmapen en downloadclients in Sonarr, Radarr en Lidarr, Prowlarr-sync, Seerr, Bazarr-koppeling en startconfiguraties voor Recyclarr en NeutArr. Instellingen → Usenet bewaart de nieuwsserver en stuurt die naar SABnzbd en NZBGet. Prowlarr krijgt ook een startset publieke indexers. Verwijder wat je niet wilt; ze worden niet opnieuw toegevoegd.

Houd downloads en media op hetzelfde volume, zodat voltooide bestanden kunnen hardlinken.

Nog zelf af te maken:

  • Een Plex-account.
  • Het setup-token van de eerste start van NeutArr (hieronder), tot dat account bestaat.
  • Aanmelden bij Jellyfin en NZBGet. Op het LAN meldt Interface openen je al aan bij Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, qBittorrent, SABnzbd, Bazarr en Seerr als de beheerder van de manager. Publieke hostnamen tonen altijd de eigen aanmelding van de app.
  • De beheerder en de wizard van de eerste start van Seerr worden voor je afgerond vanuit die gedeelde login (via Jellyfin, of een geclaimde Plex).

VPN, Cloudflare Tunnel, Recyclarr, NeutArr en back-ups zijn optioneel.

docs.title: Setup-token van de eerste start van NeutArr
docs.text:
De eerste keer dat NeutArr start, voordat het een account heeft, vraagt het om een eenmalig setup-token.

  1. Wacht tot NeutArr actief is.
  2. Open Catalogus → NeutArr → Instellingen.
  3. Kopieer Token voor de eerste start en plak het in het setupscherm van NeutArr.

Die waarde is het bestand /config/neutarr/.setup-token in het apparaat (de hostmap die als /config is gemount). NeutArr verwijdert het bestand nadat het account is aangemaakt, en het veld in Instellingen wordt leeg. Tot NeutArr is gestart, blijft het veld leeg.

De poort van de manager zelf is compose/env (AMM_API_PORT), te zien bij Instellingen → Systeem

Als Interface openen faalt:

docs.title: Instellingen die je echt gebruikt
docs.text:
Namen in de interface kunnen kort zijn; dit is wat ze in de praktijk betekenen.

Onderdeel Waarom het ertoe doet Account Gebruikersnaam, e-mail en wachtwoord van de beheerder. Apps met een lokale login gebruiken hetzelfde account Weergave Thema, accent, achtergrond, titel, icoon in de balk, aanmeldlogo en favicon Systeem Tijdzone, logniveau, PUID/PGID en de AIO-versie. Opslagpaden staan hier; mounts wijzig je in compose, niet in dit scherm. De luisterpoort van de manager is alleen compose/env Updates Updates van geïnstalleerde apps controleren en toepassen, één voor één of allemaal. Schema’s staan standaard uit. Een nieuwere AIO-image is alleen een melding — ophalen en opnieuw aanmaken op de host Back-ups Config-back-up, controleren, herstellen per app en een schema Netwerk VPN voor qBittorrent, Prowlarr en Flaresolverr (Usenet blijft erbuiten), met een lokale DNS-cache voor die apps zodat korte tunnelhaperingen Prowlarr-indexers niet offline gooien; Cloudflare Tunnel (start na de apps bij boot); publieke subdomeinen; en vertrouwde proxy’s Meldingen Discord-webhook en e-mail als een app blijft crashen, de VPN of tunnel wegvalt, er een update is, of een schijf over 90% vol is Usenet Nieuwsserver (host, poort, SSL, login, verbindingen), gestuurd naar SABnzbd en NZBGet. NZB-indexers voeg je toe in Prowlarr Startpagina Aanmeldtekst, app-balk en Jellyfin- / Seerr-API-sleutels als Start ze niet kan lezen Diagnose Waarom een Start-widget leeg is. API-sleutels worden nooit getoond. Ondersteuningslink is tijdelijke hulp op afstand — laat die uit, tenzij je samen met iemand die je vertrouwt aan het debuggen bent

docs.text: Probleem Probeer dit Leeg scherm of aanmeldlus bij een app Wis de sitegegevens van die URL; controleer of de app draait NeutArr vraagt om een setup-token Catalogus → NeutArr → Instellingen nadat NeutArr draait. Het token verdwijnt zodra het NeutArr-account bestaat Rechtenfouten bij het schrijven van bestanden De eigenaar van de hostmap moet overeenkomen met de containergebruiker (PUID/PGID) Sonarr importeert maar kopieert bestanden Downloads en media moeten één bestandssysteem delen voor hardlinks Werkt thuis, niet op mobiele data Tunnel nodig (+ bij voorkeur Access); LAN-IP’s zijn niet bereikbaar via mobiele data Twee Sonarrs die botsen Verwijder een extra Sonarr-container; alleen AIO mag hem draaien De servergrafiek telt alleen deze container Mount host-/sys alleen-lezen op /host/sys en maak opnieuw aan (Docker) Recent toegevoegd van Jellyfin lijkt kort Scroll de rij — er worden meer pagina’s geladen. Blijft de rij leeg, zet dan een Jellyfin-API-sleutel bij Instellingen → Startpagina Recent toegevoegd van Plex stopt bij 20 Die lijst is de laatste 20 van Plex qBittorrent / Prowlarr / Flaresolverr blijven gestopt na boot VPN staat aan zonder live handshake. Kijk bij Instellingen → Netwerk; AIO probeert de tunnel opnieuw en start die apps als hij omhoog is. Een handmatige VPN-Stop annuleert die poging Prowlarr-indexers niet beschikbaar / RSS-fouten Vaak een DNS-timeout via de VPN. Maak na een AIO-update de container opnieuw aan, klik daarna Test All in Prowlarr (en test opnieuw in Sonarr/Radarr) zodat de oude fout-backoff weg is. Een debug-share toont hits van de VPN-DNS-cache en fouten per resolver cloudflared logt connection refused bij boot Verwacht op oudere images toen de tunnel vóór de apps startte. Huidige images starten Cloudflare als laatste; maak opnieuw aan vanaf een actuele nightly / latest
